gen-righteous-gf-radio-canada: Righteous bends thin steel-rod letters around bowls that fill the line, while Radio Canada keeps its curves open and its lowercase standing tall. One shouts with fun, the other just talks.
gen-righteous-gf-readex-pro: Readex Pro sets broad gaps at its terminals and a tiny gap between lowercase and caps, a sans-serif made for steady reading. And Righteous, with its commanding rod-bent bowls, only adds a loud, playful voice on top.
gen-righteous-gf-roboto: Loud, round, and playful up top. Righteous packs heavy bowls into every line with a commanding swagger, while Roboto answers with low-contrast, generous-mouthed rounds that make a sans-serif body feel easy and clean.
gen-righteous-gf-ruda: Thin steel rod, bent into bowls that fill the line: that is Righteous. Ruda sits below as a wire-like monoline sans-serif with a sizable x-height and wide-mouthed rounds, so the loud heading hands off to something friendly.
gen-righteous-gf-saira: Righteous presses its strokes like twine into a flat surface, with bowls that fill the line and a commanding, fun streak. Saira takes over for the reading, with see-through s shapes and rounded letters stretching high, quiet and clean.
gen-righteous-gf-sarpanch: Sarpanch keeps its lowercase e clearly open and its gap between x-height and ascender line compact, which feels approachable and current. And Righteous, drawn as if by a fixed-width nib, is the loud, fun counterpart overhead.
gen-righteous-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Commanding Righteous fills each line with bowls drawn at the same weight as its diagonals, a fun display voice. Schibsted Grotesk follows with big open e and a shapes and terminals that never close in, easy across a whole page.
gen-righteous-gf-sen: Modern in mood, Sen builds its lowercase tall with constant weight, and curved strokes that end before turning inward. Righteous, bent from thin steel rod with bowls filling the line, supplies the fun above it.
gen-righteous-gf-sintony: Bent-paperclip strokes with no thick-thin shifts give Righteous its look, and its bowls fill the line with a commanding, fun air. Sintony does the quieter job, a chunky, tall midzone that reads smooth without clogging.
gen-righteous-gf-sofia-sans: Rod-bent and brash, Righteous fills the line with bowls, a commanding fun heading. Sofia Sans has no thick-and-thin modulation at all, and its tall lowercase looks like cut acrylic stencil pieces.
